alex: quick heads-up — hitting inconsistent cancel behavior across SDKs when cancelling streaming requests + retries. node abort -> immediate error, python abort -> hangs and runtime finishes generation (wasted tokens). anyone seen this?

rachel: can you drop a minimal repro and env (sdk versions)?

alex: repros below (node / python). node: `const ac = new AbortController(); fetch(..., { signal: ac.signal }); ac.abort()` then streaming callback gets 'aborted' almost immediately. python: `client.stream(..., timeout=5)` then calling `cancel()` on the iterator doesn't stop server generation until connection fully closes.

alex: node snippet:
```js
const c = new AbortController();
const res = await client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-1', messages }, { signal: c.signal });
res.on('data', chunk => { /* process */ });
setTimeout(() => c.abort(), 1000);
```

alex: python snippet:
```py
with client.chat.stream(model='redwood-1', messages=msgs) as stream:
    for chunk in stream:
        if should_cancel():
            stream.cancel()  # currently waits until server ends
```

sam: this matches what i saw in a smoke test. quick notes: node path uses fetch/AbortController which signals the http client and we close the TCP/stream; python's streaming iterator wraps httpx streaming and we only close the generator locally but we don't send the "stop generation" control to the runtime. runtime keeps producing until it notices socket close or times out.

jin: runtime perspective: we can react to connection close vs explicit cancel message. explicit is better for avoiding wasted compute. we expose a STOP frame over websocket and a cancel RPC for http streaming. SDKs need to call that on client-side cancel.

alex: ok — sounds like the actionable items are: 1) SDKs should emit explicit cancel/stop to runtime when client abort/cancel invoked, 2) SDKs should abort underlying transport (close socket) as fallback, 3) retries should not automatically requeue in-flight cancelled requests (or at least mark them as client-aborted so runtime ignores).

rachel: can someone sketch a small checklist we can use for PR reviews and release notes? e.g., what to test in integration.

sam: draft checklist:
- unit: AbortController/cancel API triggers transport-level abort (node/python)
- integration: cancel during token stream sends STOP control (verify runtime saw cancel)
- billing: runtime emits cancelled-vs-completed metric for token accounting
- retry behavior: client does not retry after explicit cancel; any queued retries should be opt-in
- docs: document semantics for streaming cancel + examples in node/python

jin: add: ensure websocket vs http behavior consistent; test both with short-lived and long-lived responses. also ensure we propagate a cancel reason header/field so runtime can log why it was stopped.

alex: @sam can you open a PR for node + python quick fixes? small patches: node already does both transport + stop, python needs stop + transport close. include integration test that asserts runtime token count unchanged after cancel.

sam: will do, pinging @rachel for code review when ready. PR will reference issue #1423. (reaction) :eyes:

rachel: thanks — will review. also we should surface guidance in SDK README about recommended cancel patterns and how they map to server behavior.

devex-bot: created issue <https://tracker/redwood/1423|#1423> "unified streaming cancel semantics across SDKs"

alex: great, thanks team. i'll add a short note in the release checklist to verify token accounting for cancelled streams.
